promotionalText: Your Unraid server in your pocket. Array health, disks, Docker, virtual machines and the self-hosted services running beside them. No account, no cloud.
description:
Tower is a native iOS client for your Unraid server. It talks straight to your own machine — there is no account to create, no service in the middle, and nothing of yours on anybody else's computer.

Tower does not provide, host, stream, or download any media. It is a remote management interface for a server and the applications you already run on your own hardware. A search you start runs against the indexers you configured on that server, and the result goes to your own download client. No media file is ever downloaded to your phone.

YOUR SERVER, AT A GLANCE
• Array status, capacity, and parity state the moment you open the app
• CPU, memory, uptime, per-disk temperature and usage
• User shares with their allocation settings, disks and the pool they live on
• Notifications and system logs without reaching for a terminal

DOCKER AND VIRTUAL MACHINES
• Containers with real state — start, stop, restart, pause, resume
• Per-container logs, ports, and the volumes actually mounted
• Virtual machines, including force stop when a guest stops listening
• A container and the service it runs, cross-linked both ways

CONTROL THE SERVICES YOU RUN ALONGSIDE IT
Tower drives the self-hosted applications on that server too, each through its own local API, and each appearing only once you have given Tower its address:
• Sonarr, Radarr and Lidarr: library, calendar and history; add, edit or remove a movie, series or artist; start a search and send a result to your own download client
• NZBGet: queue, progress and speeds; pause, resume or remove a download; retry from history
• Prowlarr: indexer health, and adding, testing, enabling and removing indexers
• Bazarr: subtitle status, and a manual subtitle search your server carries out
• Overseerr: search, request, and approve or decline what is waiting on you
• Tautulli: who is watching what, with bandwidth and transcoding at a glance

Tower sends the instruction; the applications on your own server do the work.

BUILT FOR iPHONE AND iPAD
• Adaptive layouts with proper split views on iPad
• Dynamic Type, semantic colors, and system controls throughout
• Light and dark, or pin whichever you prefer

PRIVATE BY CONSTRUCTION
• Connects directly to your own machines over your own network
• Every API key is stored in the iOS keychain and sent only to the server it belongs to
• No accounts, no analytics, no ads, no telemetry, no backend of ours

TRY IT FIRST
• A built-in demo mode runs the whole app against sample data — every service, every screen — so you can see everything before pointing it at a real machine

Tower requires an Unraid server with its GraphQL API enabled, and network access to it from your device. Service features require the corresponding application to be running and reachable on your network. Tower is an independent project, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Lime Technology, Inc., Plex Inc., or the projects whose APIs it speaks.
reviewNotes:
PLEASE START HERE: Tower needs no server, account or credentials to review. It has a built-in Demo Mode.

On first launch the app shows a "Connect to Unraid" screen. Tap "Try the Demo" at the bottom. The whole app then runs offline against sample data, including every action button.

WHAT THE APP IS
Tower is a native iOS client for Unraid (unraid.net), a self-hosted server operating system, and for the applications commonly run alongside it. It is a remote control for hardware the user already owns, the phone equivalent of the web administration page that server already serves. There is no Tower account, no Tower server and no sign-up.

EVERYTHING THE APP CAN DO, IN FULL
Tower is not a read-only dashboard. It can start a search on the user's own server and hand a result to that user's own download client. Every item below is reachable in Demo Mode on first launch. There are no feature flags, no remote configuration and no hidden gestures, and the app's test hooks are compiled out of shipped builds.

Unraid itself:
- Array status and capacity, parity state, CPU, memory, uptime, per-disk temperature
- Docker containers: start, stop, restart, pause, resume; logs, ports, volumes
- Virtual machines: state and power actions, including force stop
- User shares, notifications and system logs

Applications on that same server, each through its own local API:
- Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr: library, calendar and history; add, edit or delete a movie, series or artist; start an automatic search; run an interactive search and send a chosen result to the user's download client
- Prowlarr: indexer health; add, test, enable, disable or delete an indexer
- NZBGet: queue with progress and speeds; pause, resume, remove; priority and speed limit; retry from history
- Bazarr: subtitle status, and a manual subtitle search and download performed by Bazarr on the server
- Overseerr: search, submit a request, approve or decline requests, comment on issues
- Tautulli: who is watching, with bandwidth and transcoding

CONTENT AND MEDIA
Every indexer, download client and library named above is one the user configured on their own server before installing Tower. Tower ships no indexers, search engines or content sources of its own, and it downloads, saves, converts, streams and plays nothing: no media file ever reaches the iPhone or iPad, and the app has no media player and no media storage. All searching and transferring happens on the user's own machine. Tower does not access Apple Music, YouTube, SoundCloud, Vimeo or any comparable service. Posters and covers load directly from the image hosts the user's services point to, such as TMDb and TheTVDB; Tower neither sources nor redistributes them.

DEVICES AND OS TESTED BEFORE SUBMISSION
- iPhone 16 Pro Max, iOS 26.6 (physical device, via TestFlight)
- iPad, model MD3Y4LL/A, iPadOS 26.6 (physical device, via TestFlight)

EXTERNAL SERVICES, TOOLS AND PLATFORMS
None operated by us; Tower has no backend. Posters and covers load directly from the image hosts the user's services point to, such as TMDb and TheTVDB. Everything else goes only to servers the user supplies the address for. There is no analytics, crash reporting, advertising, tracking, payment processing or third-party authentication, and no App Tracking Transparency prompt. The only third-party code is Apollo iOS, an open-source GraphQL client. Credentials are held in the iOS Keychain and sent only to that user's own server. Demo Mode stores nothing and makes no network connection.

PERMISSIONS
None requested: no camera, contacts, location, photo library or microphone. Connecting to a real server triggers the standard iOS Local Network prompt; Demo Mode does not.

REGIONAL DIFFERENCES, REGULATED INDUSTRY, PROTECTED MATERIAL
None apply. English-only, identical in every region, and a server administration tool.
